title: Sales by Day of the Week
statement:
A shop records its orders and its catalogue:

- `Orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date, item_id, quantity)`: a customer ordered `quantity` units of item `item_id` on `order_date`. `(order_id, item_id)` is unique, and every `item_id` exists in `Items`.
- `Items(item_id, item_name, item_category)`: one row per item; `item_id` is unique. Several items can share a category.

Build a sales report with one row per category that appears in `Items` and the columns `Category`, `Monday`, `Tuesday`, `Wednesday`, `Thursday`, `Friday`, `Saturday` and `Sunday`. Each day column holds the total `quantity` ordered in that category on that day of the week, across all weeks. A category with no orders on a day shows `0` there, and a category whose items were never ordered still appears with seven zeros.

Order the rows by `Category` ascending.
reference:
WITH sales AS (
  SELECT i.item_category AS category, DAYNAME(o.order_date) AS weekday, o.quantity
  FROM Items AS i
  LEFT JOIN Orders AS o
    ON o.item_id = i.item_id
)
SELECT
  category AS Category,
  SUM(IF(weekday = 'Monday', quantity, 0)) AS Monday,
  SUM(IF(weekday = 'Tuesday', quantity, 0)) AS Tuesday,
  SUM(IF(weekday = 'Wednesday', quantity, 0)) AS Wednesday,
  SUM(IF(weekday = 'Thursday', quantity, 0)) AS Thursday,
  SUM(IF(weekday = 'Friday', quantity, 0)) AS Friday,
  SUM(IF(weekday = 'Saturday', quantity, 0)) AS Saturday,
  SUM(IF(weekday = 'Sunday', quantity, 0)) AS Sunday
FROM sales
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY Category;
brute:
SELECT
  c.item_category AS Category,
  (SELECT IFNULL(SUM(o.quantity), 0) FROM Orders o, Items i WHERE i.item_id = o.item_id AND i.item_category = c.item_category AND WEEKDAY(o.order_date) = 0) AS Monday,
  (SELECT IFNULL(SUM(o.quantity), 0) FROM Orders o, Items i WHERE i.item_id = o.item_id AND i.item_category = c.item_category AND WEEKDAY(o.order_date) = 1) AS Tuesday,
  (SELECT IFNULL(SUM(o.quantity), 0) FROM Orders o, Items i WHERE i.item_id = o.item_id AND i.item_category = c.item_category AND WEEKDAY(o.order_date) = 2) AS Wednesday,
  (SELECT IFNULL(SUM(o.quantity), 0) FROM Orders o, Items i WHERE i.item_id = o.item_id AND i.item_category = c.item_category AND WEEKDAY(o.order_date) = 3) AS Thursday,
  (SELECT IFNULL(SUM(o.quantity), 0) FROM Orders o, Items i WHERE i.item_id = o.item_id AND i.item_category = c.item_category AND WEEKDAY(o.order_date) = 4) AS Friday,
  (SELECT IFNULL(SUM(o.quantity), 0) FROM Orders o, Items i WHERE i.item_id = o.item_id AND i.item_category = c.item_category AND WEEKDAY(o.order_date) = 5) AS Saturday,
  (SELECT IFNULL(SUM(o.quantity), 0) FROM Orders o, Items i WHERE i.item_id = o.item_id AND i.item_category = c.item_category AND WEEKDAY(o.order_date) = 6) AS Sunday
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT item_category FROM Items) AS c
ORDER BY c.item_category
notes:
## Intuition

This is a pivot: categories become rows and the seven weekdays become columns. Each output cell is a sum of quantities restricted to one day, which a conditional aggregate expresses directly: `SUM(IF(day matches, quantity, 0))`. Because every category in `Items` must appear, even one that sold nothing, the rows have to start from `Items` and attach orders with a **left join**.

## Approach

1. In the CTE `sales`, left join `Items` to `Orders` on `item_id` and keep each order's `category`, its `weekday` name from `DAYNAME(order_date)` and its `quantity`. An item with no orders gives one row whose `weekday` and `quantity` are null.
2. Group `sales` by `category`.
3. For each weekday, sum `quantity` only on rows whose `weekday` matches and add 0 otherwise; null weekdays match nothing, so unsold categories get 0 everywhere.
4. Order by `Category`.

## Example 1, step by step

`sales` holds: Book/Monday/10 (orders 1 and 2), Book/Tuesday/5, Book/Friday/10, Phone/Wednesday/5, Phone/Thursday/1, Phone/Sunday/5 (orders 8 and 9), Glasses/Friday/5, and T-shirt/null/null for the unsold T-shirt item. Grouping gives Book = 20, 5, 0, 0, 10, 0, 0; Glasses = 5 on Friday only; Phone = 5 on Wednesday, 1 on Thursday and 10 on Sunday; T-shirt = all zeros. Sorted by category this is Book, Glasses, Phone, T-shirt.

## Complexity

- Time: O(I + O) for I items and O orders with a hash join, plus O(C log C) to sort C categories.
- Space: O(I + O) for the joined rows, O(C) for the groups.

## Pitfalls

- An inner join drops categories with no orders; the report must still list them with zeros.
- `DAYOFWEEK` counts Sunday as 1 and Monday as 2, while `WEEKDAY` counts Monday as 0; mixing them shifts every column by one day.
- `SUM(IF(..., quantity, NULL))` returns null for an empty day; use 0 as the else value.
- Grouping by `item_id` or `item_name` instead of the category splits a category into several rows.

## Clauses

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `i` | `Items`, so every category is present |
| `o` | `Orders`, attached by `item_id` (null when an item never sold) |
| `sales` | one row per order (or unsold item): `category`, `weekday`, `quantity` |
| `SUM(IF(weekday = ..., quantity, 0))` | the units of one category sold on one weekday |

narration.1: The sales CTE gathers one row per order with its category and day name.
narration.2: DAYNAME turns each order date into a weekday name such as Monday.
narration.4: A left join from Items keeps categories whose items were never ordered.
narration.9: Each day column sums only the quantities of rows on that weekday and adds 0 for the rest.
narration.17: One group per category gives one report row.
narration.18: The report is sorted by category name.
